explanation: Germans are direct communicators, so a clear, polite decline - ideally with a short reason like being full - is generally respected and taken at face value; hosts typically won't keep pressing you to eat more, unlike in some hospitality-insistent cultures. A vague or hesitant 'no' offered just to seem polite can backfire, since it may be read as your real answer and nothing more will be offered.
local_tip: If you don't want more food, say so plainly once - there's no need for an elaborate excuse, since a direct 'no' is taken seriously rather than as modesty.

also_check.note: A polite refusal out of modesty is common, but hosts may still insist once or twice before accepting it.
Refusing home-cooked food can be taken personally, since it's seen as rejecting the host's hospitality and effort.
Hosts often insist multiple times before accepting a refusal, though stated dietary restrictions are generally respected.
